mainTopic: Paying a מודר's debt according to חנן or everyone, and returning a lost item when a נדר forbids benefit
overview: The משנה allowed a person to pay off the debt of someone who is forbidden by a נדר to benefit from him. רב הושעיא explains that this follows חנן, who holds that paying someone else's obligation without being asked is not a real benefit to him. רבא says everyone could agree, if the loan was given on condition that it need not be repaid. The גמרא quotes the משנה where חנן argues with the בני כהנים גדולים about a man who supported another man's wife while her husband was overseas. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי praises חנן's view. The גמרא then explains why רבא and רב הושעיא each kept his own explanation: רב הושעיא worries about a גזירה, because a no-repayment loan could be confused with a normal one. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that one may return a lost item. רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue whether this is allowed even when the returner is the forbidden one, because of the 'פרוטה of רב יוסף'.

steps.title: The ruling follows חנן
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא answers the challenge from the previous עמוד: the משנה's ruling, that one may pay the debt of the מודר, follows the opinion of חנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the opinion of חנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the question of how the משנה can allow paying the debt of someone forbidden by vow to benefit from you. He says that ruling matches the view of חנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנן holds that if you pay someone's debt without being asked, you get nothing back from him. So paying the debt is not counted as giving him real benefit, and it is allowed even under the נדר. The point is that the ruling may not be accepted by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinion is that one who pays another's expenses without being asked loses his money

phrases.english: It is the opinion of Ḥanan.
phrases.notes: This is רב הושעיא finishing his answer from the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf about paying the debt of a מודר הנאה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's permission to pay the מודר's debt follows חנן

steps.title: רבא: Everyone can agree in a special loan case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ruling can fit everyone's opinion if the loan was given on condition that the borrower need not repay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say this is everyone's opinion. It is talking about a מודר הנאה who was given a loan on the condition that he does not have to repay it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different way to read the משנה, so that it does not depend only on חנן. He sets up a special kind of loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender agreed that the borrower never has to pay him back, the borrower owes nothing for real. So someone who pays that 'debt' gives the borrower no true benefit. That makes it permitted even according to the בני כהנים גדולים who argue with חנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A person forbidden by a נדר from benefiting from someone

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה's ruling does not force us to follow only חנן. Everyone accepts it in this special case.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it is everyone's opinion,
regarding one forbidden by vow to benefit
who was given a loan on condition not to repay.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to make the ruling fit everyone, instead of only חנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a special loan
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling only works according to חנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees when the loan need not be repaid

steps.title: What is חנן's opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where חנן's opinion comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the opinion of חנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which teaching of חנן it was talking about. This sets up the next step, where the source is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 mentioned חנן without explaining his view. Now the גמרא goes back to show the original case where חנן gave his ruling.

phrases.english: What is the opinion of Ḥanan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חנן opinion mentioned in step 1

steps.title: חנן: Supporting another man's wife loses the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone supported a man's wife while he was overseas, חנן says the supporter lost his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A man went overseas, and someone else stepped up and supported his wife. חנן said: He lost his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the משנה with חנן's ruling. A person who paid another man's obligation without being asked cannot collect it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband never asked the man to feed his wife, and never promised to pay him back. So חנן says the supporter has no claim against the husband. This is why paying someone's debt is not seen as giving him a real benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who went to a country overseas,
and someone arose and supported his wife.
Ḥanan said: He lost his money.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חנן rules that one who supports another's wife without being asked cannot collect from the husband

steps.title: The בני כהנים גדולים disagree: he swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: The בני כהנים גדולים say the supporter swears how much he spent and collects it. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס agrees with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בני כהנים גדולים argued with him and said: He swears how much he spent, and takes it. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס said: Like their words.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the other side of the argument. The supporter can get his money back after taking an oath about the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, the husband did get a benefit, because his duty to feed his wife was covered. So he must pay back. The oath is needed because the husband does not know how much was spent.

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of the כהנים גדולים, the group who argue with חנן
And he takes, meaning he collects

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. חנן says the supporter loses, and the בני כהנים גדולים say he collects.

phrases.english: The sons of High Priests disagreed with him,
and said: He swears how much he spent, and takes it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס כְּדִבְרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said: In accordance with their words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to חנן within the quoted משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The supporter swears how much he spent and collects from the husband

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי: חנן spoke well
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי sides with חנן. He says the supporter put his money in a place where it cannot be recovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי said: חנן spoke well. He put his money on the horn of a deer.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה ends with רבי יוחנן בן זכאי praising חנן's view. He uses a picture to show that the money is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money placed on a deer's horn runs off with the deer and cannot be caught. In the same way, a person who pays for someone without being asked cannot expect to get it back. This backs up חנן, whose view the גמרא used to explain the משנה in נדרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The horn of a deer, a picture of money that cannot be recovered

steps.whatToRemember: חנן holds that paying another person's obligation without being asked is a loss for the payer, and he cannot collect. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי agrees with him. That is why the משנה can let one pay a מודר's debt: it does not count as real benefit. רבא adds that in a loan given on condition not to repay, everyone agrees.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said:
Ḥanan spoke well,
he placed his money on the horn of a deer.
phrases.notes: A deer runs away fast, so money left on its horn is as good as gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: יָפֶה אָמַר חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sides with חנן against the בני כהנים גדולים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי supports חנן: one who pays without being asked loses his money

steps.title: Why רבא did not explain the משנה like רב הושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבא preferred his own explanation because it makes the משנה fit everyone's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not agree with רב הושעיא, because רבא explains our משנה so that it fits everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא did not accept רב הושעיא's explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הושעיא said the משנה follows only חנן's opinion. רבא prefers an explanation that fits all the תנאים, because then the משנה does not depend on one minority view. His case of a loan given on condition that it need not be repaid lets everyone agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets up or explains a source as talking about a specific case or opinion
According to everyone; fitting all opinions

phrases.english: Rava did not say like Rav Hoshaya,
because he explains our Mishnah
according to everyone's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing where חנן's view comes from, the גמרא explains why רבא did not use it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An explanation that fits all opinions is better than one that fits only a single תנא.

steps.title: Why רב הושעיא did not explain the משנה like רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא rejects רבא's case because the רבנן would forbid even a no-repayment loan, so that people do not confuse it with a normal loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא did not agree with רבא, because we would make a decree against a loan given on condition that it is not repaid, because of a normal loan that must be repaid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב הושעיא's reason for not accepting רבא's explanation. This finishes their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case was a loan given on condition that it does not need to be repaid. רב הושעיא says the רבנן would forbid paying even that kind of loan, so that people would not come to pay a normal loan. Since that case would also be forbidden, the משנה must follow חנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree forbidding something to protect against a real prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the משנה fits everyone, and it is talking about a loan with no duty to repay. רב הושעיא: that case is forbidden by a גזירה, so the משנה must follow חנן.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya did not say like Rava,
there is a decree against a loan given on condition that it is not repaid
phrases.notes: He means: we forbid paying even this kind of loan for him, because people could mix it up with a normal one.

phrases.english: because of a loan that must be repaid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reason, balancing step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Their argument depends on whether the רבנן would forbid even a no-repayment loan because it looks like a normal loan.

steps.title: Next line of the משנה: returning a lost item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that he may return a lost item, and says that רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He returns his lost item to him.' רבי אמי and רבי אסי argue about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. Here it is only setting up an argument; the two opinions come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows a person under a נדר to return a lost item. The question is which person is forbidden: the owner of the item, or the person returning it. רבי אמי and רבי אסי will each answer differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Returns; also, the person who returns the item

phrases.english: "He returns his lost item to him."

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi argue about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the next case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person under a נדר may return a lost item; how far this goes is argued.

steps.title: First view: allowed only when the owner is the one forbidden
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says returning is allowed only when the owner is forbidden from the returner's property. If the returner is the one forbidden, he may not return it, because of the 'פרוטה of רב יוסף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: The משנה only allows it when the returner's property is forbidden to the owner. When he returns it, he is just giving the owner back his own thing. But if the owner's property is forbidden to the returner, he may not return it, because the owner would be giving him the benefit of the 'פרוטה of רב יוסף'.
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion limits the משנה to one case: only when the owner of the lost item is the one forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving someone back his own item is not giving him anything new, so the owner gets no forbidden benefit. In the other direction, the returner does gain something: while he is busy with a מצוה, he does not have to give a coin to a poor person who asks. That small saving counts as benefit from the owner, and the נדר forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the lost item
The coin a person saves because, while busy with a מצוה, he is exempt from giving to a poor person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. 'נכסי מחזיר אסורין על בעל אבידה' means the OWNER is forbidden, and that case is fine. 'נכסי בעל אבידה אסורין על מחזיר' means the RETURNER is forbidden, and that is the case being argued.

phrases.english: One said: They only taught this

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁנִּכְסֵי מַחְזִיר אֲסוּרִין עַל בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה,
phrases.english: where the returner's property is forbidden to the owner of the lost item,
because when he returns it to him
he is returning to him something that is his own.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נִכְסֵי בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה אֲסוּרִין עַל מַחְזִיר
phrases.english: But where the owner's property is forbidden to the returner,
he may not return it to him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מְהַנֵּי לֵיהּ פְּרוּטָה דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: because the owner gives him the benefit of the peruta of Rav Yosef.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף taught that someone busy returning a lost item doesn't have to give charity right then, so the coin he saves is a gain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side of the argument introduced in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning is allowed only when the owner is the one forbidden; if the returner is forbidden, he may not return it because of the פרוטה of רב יוסף.

steps.title: Second view: allowed both ways, because the coin case is rare
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא allows returning even when the returner is the forbidden one, because the 'פרוטה of רב יוסף' situation is uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: Even when the owner's property is forbidden to the returner, he may return it. As for the פרוטה of רב יוסף, that does not happen often.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion allows returning the lost item in both cases. The גמרא gives both sides here without deciding between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view agrees that the פרוטה of רב יוסף would be a real benefit. It says we do not worry about it, because a poor person rarely asks for charity at the exact moment someone is busy with the lost item. So returning the item does not usually give the returner any gain.

keyTerms.meaning: Not common; a rare case we do not worry about

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that returning an item to an owner who is forbidden is fine. They argue only when the returner is the forbidden one. One forbids it because of the פרוטה of רב יוסף; the other allows it because that case is rare.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִכְסֵי בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה
phrases.english: And one said: Even where the owner's property
is forbidden to the returner, he returns it to him,
and as for the concern of the peruta of Rav Yosef,
it is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ נִכְסֵי בַּעַל אֲבֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 10 by setting aside the worry about the פרוטה of רב יוסף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this second view, returning a lost item is allowed even when the returner is the forbidden one, because the פרוטה of רב יוסף case rarely comes up. The גמרא does not decide between the two views.
